notes: Large-source-unit candidate reviewed and retained: בְּעֵינָיו → him writes no English for the preposition and none for עַיִן, so no morpheme owns a part of the rendering and rule 2 has no allocation to test; the single word writes the suffix's own lexeme, which makes that morpheme the uniquely defensible anchor under rule 6, as with בְּעֵינֵי פַרְעֹה → Pharaoh.
YHWH hûʾ is read as pronoun-subject plus name-predicate on the ASV's own construal, so It goes to the pronoun and the copula joins the name (rule 20).

הַטּוֹב divides into the substantival article taking what (rule 41) and the adjective taking seemeth good, seemeth being the linking verb English writes where a copula would stand (rule 20), headed on good.
לֹא takes nothing, the negation having been recast onto the object nominal (rule 15); the article of כָּל־הַדְּבָרִים is unrepresented, the ASV writing every whit with no the (rule 29).
